t: You're looking at Kent Terrace, a row of nineteenth-century houses on the edge of Regent's Park, in London NW1. The terrace was designed by John Nash, the architect behind so much of Georgian and Regency London. Nash worked in the neoclassical and picturesque styles, and his schemes were financed by the Prince Regent and by the property developer James Burton. He also worked closely with Burton's son, Decimus Burton. Take in the long, orderly run of the façade and think of it as one piece of Nash's wider plan for this part of the city.
